value.note: Operating Ratings, which the datasheet distinguishes sharply from absolute maxima: 'Electrical specifications do not apply when operating the device outside of its operating ratings' (Note 1, p.5). A 12 V input is permitted here, well above the AP2112's 6.0 V ceiling.

source.ref: Operating Ratings, p.4 — 'Supply Input Voltage (VIN) +2.5V to +12V'

value.note: The absolute-maximum supply input range is -20 V to +20 V, i.e. symmetric — the part has reversed-battery protection as a listed feature (p.1). That is unusual and worth knowing: an accidental input polarity reversal does not necessarily destroy this regulator, whereas it would kill most CMOS LDOs.

source.ref: Absolute Maximum Ratings, p.4 — 'Supply Input Voltage (VIN) -20V to +20V'; Features p.1 ('Reversed-battery protection')

value.note: The 3.3 V fixed option, e.g. MIC5219-3.3BM5 / -3.3YM5 in SOT-23-5 — the part used in the datasheet's own '3.3V Ultra-Low-Noise Regulator' application circuit on p.1. The family also offers other fixed voltages (the ordering table on p.2 lists 2.5 V and 2.85 V among them) plus an adjustable version with an ADJ feedback pin. Output accuracy is better than 1%.

source.ref: Typical Applications 3.3V circuit, p.1; Ordering Information, p.2; General Description, p.1

value.note: Dropout is strongly load-dependent on this part — a factor of eight across the load range — so a single number would be misleading. The values below are the datasheet MAXIMUM column; typicals are 10 / 115 / 175 / 350 mV respectively. The features list summarises it as 'Low 500mV maximum dropout voltage at full load'. This very low dropout at light load (10 mV typical) is the part's selling point versus the AMS1117's 1.3 V.

value.note: CRITICAL QUALIFICATION — the 500 mA figure means different things per package: 'SOT-23-5 package - 500mA PEAK; 2mm x 2mm MLF package - 500mA CONTINUOUS; 2mm x 2mm Thin MLF package - 500mA continuous; MSOP-8 package - 500mA continuous' (Features, p.1). The general description adds that in SOT-23-5 the peak rating targets start-up inrush and 'continuous output current is limited only by package and layout'. A design needing 500 mA continuously must therefore NOT use the SOT-23-5 variant. KNOWN GATE LIMITATION: because peak and continuous share the same number, a purely numeric regulator-adequacy check cannot distinguish them; separating them would need a continuous_current_ma slot. Flagged here rather than silently averaged.

source.ref: Features, p.1 (per-package peak vs continuous); General Description, p.1

value.text: A 1 uF capacitor should be placed from IN to GND if there is more than 10 inches of wire between the input and the AC filter capacitor, or if a battery is used as the input. Deliberately stored as a qualitative fact rather than an unconditional 1 uF requirement: the datasheet makes it conditional on input wiring length and source type, neither of which a schematic netlist can determine.

source.ref: Applications Information / Input Capacitor, p.9

value.note: 'An output capacitor is REQUIRED between OUT and GND to prevent oscillation. The minimum size of the output capacitor is dependent upon whether a reference bypass capacitor is used.' That coupling is the reason required_bypass_cap exists as its own slot: fitting the 470 pF bypass capacitor raises the output-capacitor minimum from 1 uF to 2.2 uF. With the bypass state unknown, on_unknown='strictest' selects 2.2 uF. A THIRD condition applies to other family members but not to this 3.3 V part: 'For applications < 3V, the output capacitor should be increased to 22uF minimum to reduce start-up overshoot.' Larger values improve transient response.

source.ref: Applications Information / Output Capacitor, p.9 — '2.2uF minimum is recommended when CBYP is 470pF'; typical application circuits p.1 show 2.2 uF tantalum
Applications Information / Output Capacitor, p.9 — '1uF minimum is recommended when CBYP is not used'
Applications Information / Output Capacitor, p.9

value.note: 470 pF from the BYP pin to GND reduces output noise; the pin may be left open. Optional in itself, but NOT free of consequence — fitting it doubles the minimum output capacitance (see required_cout). Both of the datasheet's own ultra-low-noise application circuits on p.1 fit 470 pF together with a 2.2 uF tantalum output capacitor. On the adjustable variant this pin is the ADJ feedback input instead.
